draft.title: Counter-urbanisation
card: Counter-urbanisation is the movement of people from large cities to rural areas and small towns. It runs the opposite way to the usual pull of people towards cities.
Common reasons are lifestyle, such as space, quiet and a slower pace, and cheaper housing than in the city.
Remote work is another reason. People who can do their job online do not need to live near an office.
Counter-urbanisation can bring new residents, spending and demand for services to a town. It can also push up local house prices and put pressure on services.
draft.remember: Counter-urbanisation is people moving out of cities to rural places, often for lifestyle, cheaper housing or remote work.

a.q: Which of these is an example of counter-urbanisation?
opts: A Sydney family moves to a small town near Orange
A farmer sells up and moves to Newcastle for work
A Bourke student moves to Sydney to attend university
A Melbourne family moves to an apartment in the city centre
a.why: The Sydney family is moving from a large city to a small rural town, which is counter-urbanisation. The farmer and the student move towards cities, which is the opposite direction. The apartment move stays within the city.
a.clue: Look for people moving out of a city to a rural place.

b.q: Priya works online for a Brisbane company. She moves to a small town in the Northern Rivers, where homes cost less. Which pair of reasons best explains her move?
opts: Remote work and cheaper housing
Farm mechanisation and loss of services
Closer markets and a shorter commute
Urban consolidation and public transport
b.why: Priya can do her job online, so she does not need to live in the city, and homes cost less in the town. The other pairs describe other ideas: farm change, city commuting or planning, none of which fit her case.
b.clue: Her job is online and the homes are cheaper.

a.best: A Sydney family moves to a small town near Orange

problems.detail: The clue ('Her job is online and the homes are cheaper') just restates the two reasons in the right option, so it hands students the answer without testing the idea.

The stem already says she works online and that homes cost less, so matching these to 'Remote work and cheaper housing' is too easy for Year 12. A student needs only to match words, not understand counter-urbanisation.

b.q: Over five years, many Sydney workers whose jobs went online move to a village near Bathurst. Which statement best describes this trend?
opts: Remote work lets them move, and house prices may rise
Remote work lets them move, and services may lose demand
Farm jobs draw them in, and house prices may rise
Farm jobs draw them in, and services may lose demand
b.why: Online jobs mean these workers no longer need to live near a city office, so remote work explains the move. More residents means more people wanting homes, which can push up local house prices. Services losing demand is the tempting trap: new residents add demand for services, they do not take it away.
b.clue: Think about what extra residents do to demand in a small village.
